ECE 685 | Power Systems Design L36
Power Flow V
Newton–Raphson theory
Buxin She
Mike Wiegers Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

Lecture outline
1 Scalar Newton: locate a zero using a tangent.
2 Vector Newton: solve coupled correction equations.
3 Power flow: select P/Q equations and construct the Jacobian.
Understand why the correction is needed and where every coefficient comes from.

The general Newton iteration
1 Evaluate
Calculate the original residual f(x) at the current guess.
2 Test
Accept when ‖f‖∞ = max𝑖 |𝑓𝑖| ≤ 𝜀 .
3 Solve
Build J at the same point; solve JΔx = −f.
4 Update
Add Δx and return to the original equations.
A singular Jacobian may prevent a unique step. Stop with failure at the iteration cap.
ECE 685 | Power Flow V 19/40

PART 2
Newton–Raphson power flow
We already know how to solve a zero-residual system. Now construct
that system from the network’s real and reactive power balance.

Apply the same Newton method
Part 1 gave us a method for any selected system f(x) = 0:
J(x(𝑟))Δx = −f(x(𝑟)), x(𝑟+1) = x(𝑟) + Δx.
T o apply it to a power network, identify three ingredients:
1 The unknown voltage angles and magnitudes: x.
2 The power balance equations, with all terms on one side: f.
3 The derivatives of those same residual equations: J.
Start with the physical equations. Their residuals become the input to the existing
Newton method.

ECE 685 | Power Flow V 22/40

Move the power balance to one side
At bus 𝑖, generation minus demand must equal the injection into the network:
𝑃𝐺𝑖 − 𝑃𝐷𝑖 = 𝑃 𝑖(𝜃, v), 𝑄 𝐺𝑖 − 𝑄𝐷𝑖 = 𝑄 𝑖(𝜃, v).
Define one residual for each equation:
𝑓𝑃 𝑖 = 𝑃 𝑖(𝜃, v) + 𝑃𝐷𝑖 − 𝑃𝐺𝑖 = 0 ,
𝑓𝑄𝑖 = 𝑄 𝑖(𝜃, v) + 𝑄𝐷𝑖 − 𝑄𝐺𝑖 = 0 .
Here G denotes generation and D denotes demand; positive injection is into the
network.
For a load-only bus, 𝑓𝑃 𝑖 = 𝑃 𝑖 + 𝑃 𝐷𝑖: the network injection must be negative to supply
positive demand.
Source: Glover et al., sixth edition, Secs. 6.4, 6.6; Zimmerman et al., IEEE Trans. Power Syst., 2011, Eqs. (30)–(31).

The complete Newton power flow iteration
1 Evaluate
Form the selected residuals f(x) from the original P and Q balances.
2 Test
Accept the equation solution if ‖f‖∞ ≤ 𝜀 . At the iteration cap, report
nonconvergence.
3 Solve
Build J = 𝜕 f/𝜕x at the same state. Solve JΔx = −f.
4 Update
Add the correction to the selected angles and magnitudes, then return to Step 1.
Preserve the fixed slack phasor and PV magnitudes. Use a linear-system solver; do not
explicitly form the matrix inverse.

𝑃𝐺,𝑠 = 𝑃 𝑠(x) + 𝑃𝐷,𝑠 at the slack bus 𝑠,
𝑄𝐺𝑖 = 𝑄 𝑖(x) + 𝑄𝐷𝑖 at PV and slack buses .
Now check generator reactive limits and other operating requirements.
If a PV generator reaches a Q limit, fix its Q at the limit, release its voltage
magnitude, and rebuild the selected equations as a PQ bus.
The inner Newton solve uses fixed bus types. A converged equation solution still
needs the operating checks.
Source: Glover et al., sixth edition, Sec. 6.6; Zimmerman et al., IEEE Trans. Power Syst., 2011, Sec. III-A.
